title: Chelsea fined £10.75 mn for historical financial breaches
byline: Chelsea were fined £10.75 million ($14.27 million) and received a suspended one-year transfer ban on Monday in relation to historical breaches of Premier League rules.

title: Worker arrested over molestation of German tourist at Mihintale
byline: Police have arrested an archaeological worker over the alleged molestation of a German female tourist at the historic Mihintale temple premises, police said.

title: Iran Navy Chief warns of “deadly retaliation” after sailors killed off Sri Lanka
byline: The commander of the Iranian Navy has issued a stern warning following a fatal incident in the Indian Ocean, stating that the nation’s adversaries will encounter ’’deadly retaliation’’ after several sailors were killed off the coast of Sri Lanka, according to Iranian state broadcaster Press TV.

title: Google questions maintainability of Sri Lankan Judge’s writ petition in Karnataka High Court
byline: Google and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology today questioned the maintainability of a writ petition filed in the Karnataka High Court by Sri Lankan Supreme Court Judge, Justice AHMD Nawaz, seeking deletion of certain online articles published against him.

title: MPs have to stay in queues to obtain fuel: Opposition MP
byline: Members of Parliament also stay in the queues to purchase fuel just like the general public as there is no special treatment for them, Opposition MP S.M. Marikkar said.

title: Sri Lanka turns to American gas for cooking
byline: Sri Lanka has turned to the United States for domestic gas purchases instead of depending on the Middle East for supplies, and a shipment that has already been imported is currently stored at anchorage in the Maldives waters due to the lack of sufficient storage facilities in the country, an official said.

title: Drones, rockets fired at US embassy in Baghdad, security sources say
byline: Rockets and at least five drones were ​launched at the U.S. embassy in Baghdad ‌early on Tuesday from areas around the city, Iraqi security sources said, describing the attack as the most intense since ​the start of the U.S.-Israel war with ​Iran.

title: Prices of essential food items might be increased: Minister
byline: Prices of essential food items might be increased due to the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, Minister of Trade and Food Security Wasantha Samarasinghe said.

title: Afghanistan accuses Pakistan of killing 400 in attack on Kabul hospital
byline: Afghanistan has accused Pakistan’s military of launching an air strike on a hospital treating drug users in the capital, Kabul, killing at least 400 people.

title: Sri Lanka charts course for high-end marine tourism with focus on shipwreck diving
byline: Sri Lanka is actively pivoting towards high-value, experiential travel by heavily promoting its untapped marine tourism sector, with a strategic focus on shipwreck diving.

title: Power interruptions may become necessary, Minister tells Parliament
byline: Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody told Parliament that power interruptions could become unavoidable in the future despite the government’s efforts to maintain a continuous electricity supply.

title: Government moves to regulate online marketplaces and deliveries
byline: The government would soon implement strict regulations on online businesses and courier services to safeguard consumers, Minister of Trade and Commerce Wasantha Samarasinghe said.

title: Jambo electrocuted in Mahagodayaya, Buttala
byline: The carcass of a wild elephant was recovered by Buttala police last morning from a cultivated land at Mahagodayaya in Buttala area.

title: 17-year RI for statutory rape
byline: An accused who stood indicted with statutory rape of an underage girl was found guilty and sentenced to 17 year Rigorous Imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 32500 under two counts by Galle High Court Judge Purnima Paranagama.

title: Over five million vehicles registered with QR system by now: Eranga Weeraratne
byline: Deputy Minister of Digital Economy, Eranga Weeraratne revealed today that 5,103,991 vehicles have been registered with the Fuel QR Code System so far.

title: Fuel shortage puts health services in a tight spot
byline: Health services across the country are likely to be affected due to the prevailing fuel shortage, with doctors warning that the limited fuel quota allocated under the QR code system is insufficient for them to report for duty and carry out essential medical services.

title: Trump seeks to delay meeting with Xi in China
byline: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is planning to delay a high stakes visit to China later in March by about a month because of the Iran war.

title: Archchuna demands more fuel for MPs
byline: Independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna raised concerns, claiming that the fuel quota of 15 litres is not sufficient for Parliamentarians who come from outstations to attend Parlaimentary sessions.

title: Daily Mirror report comes to limelight in Parliament
byline: The Daily Mirror report under the headline ’Court warns funds leaving Sri Lanka through Crypto currency’ came to the limelight in Parliament today when MP Ravi Karunanayake raised a question on this.

title: Police warn public against fake social media posts claiming official guidance
byline: Amid a surge of misleading information online, the Sri Lanka Police has alerted the public to fake social media posts circulating under the title “Awareness by the Sri Lanka Police Department,” which falsely claim to provide official guidance.

title: Gotabaya Rajapaksa appears before Bribery Commission
byline: Former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa appeared before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) for a statement to be recorded.

title: Teens sue Musk’s xAI over Grok’s pornographic images of them
byline: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company is facing a lawsuit from teenagers who say the company facilitated child pornography by allowing the creation of sexually explicit images of them.

title: 50 forests to be gazetted as protected areas
byline: Although this year’s International Day of Forests will not be celebrated with large-scale events, the Sri Lankan government has announced the protection of 50 additional forests under the ‘Vanaspathi’ programme, Environment Minister Dr. Dhammika Patabedi said today.

title: Ravi K, Deputy Minister clash over oral question
byline: A verbal clash erupted between MP Ravi Karunanayake and Deputy Minister of Fisheries Ratna Gamage over an oral question raised by the MP that over eight companies importing canned fish are facing closure as a result of freight increases due to the Middle Eastern conflict.

title: Diesel stocks sufficient until April 12: Minister
byline: Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody revealed that diesel stocks sufficient until April 12 are available, including fuel stocks  confirmed by the suppliers.

title: COPF recommends increment of CIABOC officials’ salaries
byline: The Committee on Public Finance (COPF) has recommended a salary hike for the officers attached to the Committee to Investigate Complaints on Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) and make it similar to that of judges.

title: Half a million USD tourism revenue at risk due to war in Middle East
byline: In the midst of escalating conflict in the Gulf, Sri Lanka’s daily tourism revenue at risk has been estimated at half million US dollars, according to a top official from the Sri Lanka Tourism, Development Authority.

title: Wednesdays off for private, international students
byline: Students of international schools, private universities, and vocational training centers across the country will now have Wednesdays off, following a new government directive aimed at conserving fuel.

title: Middle East war leaves Ella tourism zone dry
byline: Ella Tourism Zone has been in had hit owing to the Middle East military conflict, much to anxiety of thousands of people, who depended on the income from providing services to the foreign tourists.

title: Binance responds to cryptocurrency allegations
byline: In light of the media coverage concerning ongoing court proceedings in Sri Lanka related to allegations of financial fraud involving the use of Binance accounts by certain individuals, Binance, an Abu Dhabi Global Markets licensed exchange with a fully KYC-ed user base globally, said these allegations pertain solely to the actions of specific parties

title: Iran Navy Chief warns of “deadly retaliation” after sailors killed off Sri Lanka
byline: The commander of the Iranian Navy has issued a stern warning following a fatal incident in the Indian Ocean, stating that the nation’s adversaries will encounter ’’deadly retaliation’’ after several sailors were killed off the coast of Sri Lanka, according to Iranian state broadcaster Press TV.

title: Drones, rockets fired at US embassy in Baghdad, security sources say
byline: Rockets and at least five drones were ​launched at the U.S. embassy in Baghdad ‌early on Tuesday from areas around the city, Iraqi security sources said, describing the attack as the most intense since ​the start of the U.S.-Israel war with ​Iran.

title: How is Sri Lanka responding to the Israel–Iran conflict: Day 17
byline: As tensions escalate between Israel and Iran, Sri Lanka has taken a series of diplomatic, aviation and precautionary measures to manage potential fallout and safeguard its citizens. Here is how Sri Lanka is responding.

title: Four committees established to tackle impact of Middle East conflict
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal by the President to establish four special committees to address the economic and social impacts of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

title: Avurudu Nakath Seettuwa released
byline: The Avurudu Nakath Seettuwa for this year’s Sinhala and Tamil New Year has been officially released, Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs Hiniduma Sunil Senevi said.

title: Israel says it has killed Ali Larijani, Iran’s top security official
byline: Ali Larijani, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, has been according to Israel’s Defence Minister Katz. Iran has not commented on the claim.

title: Circular issued declaring every Wednesday a holiday
byline: The Public Administration Ministry has issued a circular stating that, in response to potential fuel shortages caused by the ongoing armed conflict in the Middle East, the Government will conserve fuel in the public sector by declaring every Wednesday a holiday for government offices until further notice.

title: Cabinet approves grant from India to provide electric motorcycles for fisheries field officers
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to provide electric motorcycles to field officers engaged in fisheries duties under a financial grant from the Government of India.

title: Iran renews attacks on US Gulf allies, Trump says that was not expected
byline: Iran launched fresh attacks ​on the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday, the kind of strikes on U.S. Gulf allies that President Donald Trump said had not been expected, but which sources said he had been warned about before the ‌conflict.

title: Fuel quota to expire Saturday, to be renewed Sunday
byline: The fuel quota currently available to the public will expire on Saturday night and will be renewed on Sunday, Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation, D. J. Rajakaruna said.

title: Schools to operate four days a week amid fuel crisis
byline: All government and government-approved private schools will operate only four days a week until further notice due to the ongoing global fuel crisis, the Education authorities have informed school principals.

title: Public transport to be restricted on Wednesdays
byline: Public transport services in Sri Lanka will be limited on Wednesdays declared as government public holidays,  Essential Services Commissioner General Prabath Chandrakeerthi said today.

title: No Parliament sessions tomorrow
byline: The Business Committee of Parliament has decided not to convene Parliament tomorrow as Wednessdays have been declared as a holiday by the government.

title: Jumbo electrocuted in Mahagodayaya, Buttala
byline: The carcass of a wild elephant was recovered by Buttala police last morning from a cultivated land at Mahagodayaya in Buttala area.

title: 17-year RI sentence for statutory rape
byline: An accused who stood indicted with statutory rape of an underage girl was found guilty and sentenced to 17 year Rigorous Imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 32500 under two counts by Galle High Court Judge Purnima Paranagama.

title: Middle East conflict delays crude oil shipments to Sri Lanka
byline: Delays in crude oil shipments have been reported due to the ongoing war in the Middle East, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said.

title: President’s special statement
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake holds a special press conference on Sri Lanka’s current situation

title: CSE Extends Decline Amid Heightened Volatility and Power Cut Concerns
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange experienced a highly volatile session on 17th March 2026, as early optimism quickly gave way to sharp selling pressure. The ASPI gained 263 points during the first half of the session, reflecting positive investor sentiment at the open. However, the market reversed direction sharply following the circulation of news regarding potential power cuts linked to fuel supply disruptions, ultimately closing 521 points lower.

title: Cabinet approves legal action against misuse of eZCash for Crime
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved taking legal action against individuals using eZCash and mCash money transfer systems for transactions linked to drug trafficking and organized crime.

title: EPF members to adjust appointments as Wednesdays declared public holidays
byline: Starting March 18, 2026, all Wednesdays will be considered as public holidays, a move that will affect services at the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) Divisions.

title: President calls for practical fuel conservation plans across ministries
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake today (17) instructed all ministries to develop practical, sustainable, and data-driven plans for fuel conservation to ensure minimal energy consumption across public and private sectors.

title: Cuba suffers nationwide blackout as fuel supplies dwindle
byline: Cuba’s electric grid suffered a total collapse Monday as the nation struggles with crumbling infrastructure and a de facto US oil blockade that’s pushed the communist-run island to the brink.

title: Key measures discussed to sustain air services amid fuel concerns
byline: A high-level meeting took place today (17) at the Civil Aviation Authority premises, chaired by Deputy Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Janitha Ruwan Kodithuwakku, to address strategies for sustaining air services amid fuel supply disruptions caused by the ongoing war situation.

title: Iran conflict could lead to severe hunger for 45 million by June, says World Food Programme
byline: The World Food Programme has warned that the ongoing conflict in Iran could result in severe hunger for approximately 45 million people by June. According to Jin10, the organization highlighted the escalating humanitarian crisis as a direct consequence of the war, emphasizing the urgent need for international intervention and support.

title: President to make special statement in Parliament on Friday
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is to make a special statement in Parliament on Friday, Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake announced today.

title: Death penalty affirmed in heroin case heard by present CJ as High Court Judge
byline: The Supreme Court today affirmed the death sentence imposed on an accused by the Colombo High Court in 2013 for possession and trafficking of 34.32 grams of heroin.

title: President invites TPA for urgent meeting
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has invited the Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA) for an urgent meeting next week, extending the invitation to TPA Leader Mano Ganesan, MP, during a phone conversation.

title: Ravi K questions Government on cryptocurrency oversight
byline: MP Ravi Karunanayake today pressed the Finance Minister in Parliament over Sri Lanka’s regulatory stance and oversight failures in cryptocurrency and digital asset transactions.

title: Cabinet nod for $620 Mn ADB deal to drive 2026 reforms
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to secure US$620 million in policy-based financing from the Asian Development Bank for 2026, aimed at advancing Sri Lanka’s ongoing reform programme.

title: Top US counterterrorism official resigns over Iran war, urging Trump to ’reverse course’
byline: The Trump administration’s top official on counterterrorism has resigned from his position, citing opposition to the war in Iran, and urged the president to ’’reverse course’’.

title: Cabinet approves legal action against misuse of eZCash and mCash for Crime
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved taking legal action against individuals using eZCash and mCash money transfer systems for transactions linked to drug trafficking and organized crime.
